A bill for an act relating to veterans; waiving parking fees at Minneapolis-St. Paul International Airport for a veteran with a total service-connected disability; proposing coding for new law in Minnesota Statutes, chapter 473.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF MINNESOTA:

Section 1.

[+[473.687] PARKING FEES WAIVED FOR DISABLED VETERANS. +]

[+Subdivision 1.+]

[+Definition.+]

[+For purposes of this section, "veteran with a total service-connected disability" means a veteran as defined in section 197.447 who has a permanent and total service-connected disability as certified by the United States Veterans Administration. +]

[+Subd. 2.+]

[+Parking fees waived for disabled veterans.+]

[+(a) Beginning January 1, 2027, a veteran with a total service-connected disability may park free of charge for up to ten consecutive or nonconsecutive days during a 90-day period at all parking facilities at the Minneapolis-St. Paul International Airport. A veteran with a total service-connected disability must be charged the standard rate for parking for any additional days of parking during the 90-day period. +]

[+(b) On or before December 1, 2026, the commission must establish a process to waive or abate fees incurred by a veteran with a total service-connected disability at all parking facilities at the Minneapolis-St. Paul International Airport. The commission must conduct outreach with veterans organizations statewide on the process and must post the process on the Minneapolis-St. Paul International Airport website. +]

[+Subd. 3.+]

[+Documentation required.+]

[+To qualify for the parking fee waiver or abatement under this section, a veteran with a total service-connected disability must provide one of the following forms of documentation at the time and in the form and manner consistent with the process established by the commission under subdivision 2: +]

[+(1) a driver's license with a graphic or written designation of "Veteran 100% T&P" under section 171.07, subdivision 15; +]

[+(2) a military identification card issued by the United States Department of Defense indicating a 100 percent disability rating; or +]

[+(3) a letter from the United States Department of Veteran Affairs confirming the veteran's 100 percent disability rating. +]

[+EFFECTIVE DATE.+]

[+This section is effective the day following final enactment. +]
bill_text.plain_text:
A bill for an act relating to veterans; waiving parking fees at Minneapolis-St. Paul International Airport for a veteran with a total service-connected disability; proposing coding for new law in Minnesota Statutes, chapter 473.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF MINNESOTA:

Section 1.

[473.687] PARKING FEES WAIVED FOR DISABLED VETERANS.

Subdivision 1.

Definition.

For purposes of this section, "veteran with a total service-connected disability" means a veteran as defined in section 197.447 who has a permanent and total service-connected disability as certified by the United States Veterans Administration.

Subd. 2.

Parking fees waived for disabled veterans.

(a) Beginning January 1, 2027, a veteran with a total service-connected disability may park free of charge for up to ten consecutive or nonconsecutive days during a 90-day period at all parking facilities at the Minneapolis-St. Paul International Airport. A veteran with a total service-connected disability must be charged the standard rate for parking for any additional days of parking during the 90-day period.

(b) On or before December 1, 2026, the commission must establish a process to waive or abate fees incurred by a veteran with a total service-connected disability at all parking facilities at the Minneapolis-St. Paul International Airport. The commission must conduct outreach with veterans organizations statewide on the process and must post the process on the Minneapolis-St. Paul International Airport website.

Subd. 3.

Documentation required.

To qualify for the parking fee waiver or abatement under this section, a veteran with a total service-connected disability must provide one of the following forms of documentation at the time and in the form and manner consistent with the process established by the commission under subdivision 2:

(1) a driver's license with a graphic or written designation of "Veteran 100% T&P" under section 171.07, subdivision 15;

(2) a military identification card issued by the United States Department of Defense indicating a 100 percent disability rating; or

(3) a letter from the United States Department of Veteran Affairs confirming the veteran's 100 percent disability rating.

EFFECTIVE DATE.

This section is effective the day following final enactment.
